title: Injectivity of the Razborov encoding on bad restrictions
statement: Fix a DNF formula $f$ on $n$ variables and parameters $w, d \in \bbn$, and suppose that $f$ has width at most $w$ and that no term of $f$ repeats a variable — within any single term, two literals sharing the same variable are identical. Under these hypotheses the Razborov encoding with parameters $w$ and $d$ is injective on the restrictions that are bad for $f$ at depth $d$: if $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are restrictions, each bad for the Boolean function computed by $f$ at depth $d$ (that is, the corresponding restricted function has decision-tree depth exceeding $d$), and their Razborov encodings agree, then $\rho_1 = \rho_2$.
hypotheses_covered: f has width at most w
no term of f repeats a variable
ρ₁ is bad for f's Boolean function at depth d
ρ₂ is bad for f's Boolean function at depth d
the Razborov encodings of ρ₁ and ρ₂ agree
replaced:
The Razborov encoding is injective on bad restrictions: for a width-$w$ DNF $f$ with
distinct variables per term, if $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are both bad restrictions for
$f.\mathrm{eval}$ at depth $d$ and their encodings agree,
$\mathrm{razborovEncode}\ f\ w\ d\ \rho_1 = \mathrm{razborovEncode}\ f\ w\ d\ \rho_2$,
then $\rho_1 = \rho_2$.
